items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to evaluating the effects
adjustments or reductions to the state budget will have on reducing child
poverty in New York state; to establish the child poverty reduction advisory
council to effectuate a reduction in child poverty in the state; and providing
for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Add Art 19-I §§533 - 533-g, Exec L; amd §§22 & 23, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2755

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to evaluating the
effects adjustments or reductions to the state budget will have on
reducing child poverty in New York state; to establish the child poverty
reduction advisory council to effectuate a reduction in child poverty in
the state; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expira-
tion thereof

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To create mechanisms and an advisory council to ensure that New York
State reduces the overall child poverty rate by fifty percent in the
next ten years.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: States legislative purpose of the bill and declares New York
shall reduce the overall child poverty rate by fifty percent in the next
ten years by creating a child poverty reduction advisory council. The
council will research policy ideas, develop best practices, and contin-
ually monitor relevant benchmarks to ensure that New York reduces child
poverty by fifty percent.

Section 2: Amends subdivision 7 of section 23 of the state finance law
by adding paragraph g to ensure before any reductions or adjustments are
made by budget director an evaluation will be made on the effects on
child poverty in New York. Such evaluations will be made available to
the public.

Section 3: Establishes "Child Poverty Reduction Advisory Council" to
effectuate a reduction in child poverty. The advisory council shall be
chaired by executive chamber and the commissioner of the office of chil-
dren and family services. Advisory council make up, rules, and roles
shall be established in this section.

Section 4: Creates appointment regulations in terms of process, dead-
lines, and what to do if there are vacancies.

Section 5: The advisory council shall develop a timeline with benchmarks
to reduce child poverty by fifty percent in ten years.  They will create
a report which reviews current policy and makes recommendations for how
to reduce childhood poverty in New York. Such reviews will include:
expanding the state's earned income and child tax credit; expanding work
training and employment programs; expanding access to childcare and
housing vouchers; and other policies. Also the advisory council will
release bi annual reports detailing the progress the state is making in
reducing the child poverty rate.

Section 6: Agencies shall take actions to implement recommendations of
the advisory council. The recommendations of the advisory council may be
overridden by a concurrent resolution.

Section 7: Department of children and family services staff shall
provide support to the advisory council.

Section 8: All meetings of the advisory committee shall be subject to
public officers law.

Section 9: If any piece of this law is unconstitutional, the court can
invalidate that clause and the rest of the legislation shall remain in
affect.

Section 10: This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and
be deemed repealed ten years after such effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Nearly 3 million New Yorkers are living in poverty, 895,000 of which are
children. In fact, 1 in 5 New York children struggle to meet basic
needs. Although legislative and administrative efforts have been under-
taken, the overall poverty rate in New York has remained the same over
the last decade. Meanwhile, the federal government continues to slash
benefits that have been shown to have positive impacts on lifting chil-
dren and their families out of poverty.

Over the next decade, this legislation aims to reduce the child poverty
rate by fifty percent. Reducing child poverty will protect the health
and general wellbeing of all New Yorkers, grow our economy, and lead to
long term savings for New York's budget. To make sure this reduction in
child poverty happens, this legislation creates the "child poverty
reduction advisory council". The council shall explore expanding specif-
ic policies, making new recommendations, and publish benchmarks, time-
lines, and reports to make sure that New York State meets the goal of
reducing child poverty by 50% in a decade.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

poverty reduction act and establishing an advisory council to effectuate

in reducing child poverty and evaluating the effects adjustments or

executive law. Section 533 reads as follows:

Sect 533-a. Declares New York shall reduce the overall child poverty
rate by 50% in the next 10 years by creating a child poverty reduction
advisory council.

Sect 533-b. Establishes "Child Poverty Reduction Advisory Council" to
effectuate a reduction in child poverty. The advisory council will be
chaired by a representative of the executive chamber and the commission-
er of the office of children and family services.  Establishes the advi-
sory council make up, rules, and roles.

Sect 533-c. Creates appointment regulations in terms of process, dead-
lines, and what to do if there are vacancies.

Sect 533-d. The advisory council shall develop a timeline with bench-
marks to reduce child poverty by fifty percent in ten years.  They will
create a report which reviews current policy and makes recommendations
for how to reduce childhood poverty in New York. Such reviews will
include: expanding the state's earned income and child tax credit;

childcare and housing vouchers; and other policies. Also the advisory
council will release bi annual reports detailing the progress the state
is making in reducing the child poverty rate.

Sect 533-e. Agencies shall take actions to implement recommendations of
the advisory council. The recommendations of the advisory council may be
overridden by a concurrent resolution.

Sect 533-f. Dept of children and family services staff shall provide
support to the advisory council.

Sect 533-g. All meetings of the advisory committee shall be subject to
public officers law.


Section 2: Section 22 of the state finance law is amended by adding
subdivision 1-d which requires the advisory council to present a report
with recommendations on the overall child poverty rate to the comp-
troller, senate finance, the assembly ways and means, and director of
budget.

Section 3: adds a new paragraph g. To subdivision 7 of section 23, which
states the director of budget shall evaluate the effect of any pending
child poverty reduction measures taken and shall publish these evalu-
ations for the public.

Section 4: If any piece of this law is unconstitutional, the court can
invalidate that clause and the rest of the legislation shall remain in
effect.

Section 5: This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and
be deemed repealed ten years after such effective date.

needs. Although legislative and administrative efforts have been under-
taken, the overall poverty rate in New York has remained the same over
the last decade. Meanwhile, the federal government continues to slash
benefits that have been shown to have positive impacts on lifting chil-
dren and their families out of poverty.  Over the next decade, this
legislation aims to reduce the child poverty rate by fifty percent.
Reducing child poverty will protect the health and general wellbeing of
all New Yorkers, grow our economy, and lead to long term savings for New
York's budget. To make sure this reduction in child poverty happens,
this legislation creates the "child poverty reduction advisory council".
The council shall explore expanding specific policies, making new recom-
mendations, and publish benchmarks, timelines, and reports to make sure
that New York State meets the goal of reducing child poverty by 50% in a
decade.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: 59012 (RAMOS) reported to Senate Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 51 Chapter 646
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2755-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to establish-
        ing an advisory council  to  effectuate  a  reduction  in  child
        poverty  in  the  state;  and  providing  for the repeal of such
        provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill as originally passed would amend the social services law  to
create  a child poverty reduction advisory council to effectuate a fifty
percent reduction in child poverty in New York State within  ten  years.
The  Council  will consist of at least 16 members and will be co-chaired
by the Commissioner of the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance
(OTDA) and a representative from the Executive Chamber. There are nearly
an estimated 900,000 children in New York living in poverty. The  estab-
lishment  of an advisory council to address this critical issue of child
poverty in the State is consistent with OTDA's core mission  of  helping
vulnerable New Yorkers meet their essential needs.
 
  I  support  the goals of this bill as childhood poverty is a pervasive
and important issue to be addressed in New York. The work of this  coun-
cil  will  drive  forward  policy initiatives and is consistent with the
mission of OTDA and of the associated agencies.  However,  the  bill  as
written  requires  the advisory council to meet unrealistic timelines. I
have secured agreement with the Legislature to extend  the  time  frames
for the council so that it can appropriately fulfill its purpose regard-
ing  this  critical issue. On that basis of that agreement, I am pleased
to sign this bill.

  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Establishes the child poverty reduction advisory council to effectuate a fifty percent reduction of child poverty in the state within ten years.
